exposure: stages of placental abruption (Stage 0-I, Stage II, Stage III)
outcome: transfers to maternal critical care units
transfers to neonatal critical care units
cohort: The study included 150 patients who underwent cesarean delivery due to clinical suspicion of placental abruption after the 20th week of gestation.
finding: More severe stages of placental abruption (Stages II and III) were associated with elevated NLR, reduced hemoglobin and fibrinogen levels, lower Apgar scores, and a higher demand for newborn intensive care.
